- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 18-day mean, adjust down by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.0 to 1.0), model reacts with lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits short-term volatility; smooth 30d forecast by averaging with 18d history if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
